<description>
`btck_transaction_create` and `btck_block_create` ignore any bytes after the serialized object, so the object's serialized length does not match the buffer.

I return null when bytes remain, as for other malformed input, and say so in the header. Two new checks in `test_kernel` append one byte to a valid transaction and to a valid block. They fail on master and pass with the change. The other kernel tests and the unit tests pass.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
fc75592ed7 kernel: reject trailing bytes in object creation

btck_transaction_create and btck_block_create deserialize one object and
ignore any bytes that follow it. The object's serialized length then
differs from the buffer's.

I return null when bytes remain after the object, as for other malformed
input, and say so in the header. The kernel tests pass a valid
transaction and a valid block with one extra byte.
</commits>
